- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 1.0) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward adjustment by 1–2 periods.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overreact — cap forecast peak at 1.5x recent high or 1.2x prior peak.  
- In low-sentiment environments (sentiment < 0.2), model often underestimates downside risk — add 2–3% buffer to forecast lows.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show strong upward trend, model often overestimates continuation — reduce forecast slope by 15–25% in next 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.5+), model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast with 3-period moving average.
